newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dithers on human rights resolution on China.
newsitem.headline: Canada dithers on human rights resolution on China.

text.p: Canada, traditionally a co-sponsor of a U.N. resolution critical of China's human rights record, was expected to decide next week whether to back the measure this year, officials said on Thursday.
"We have to assess the situation and I have to discuss that with my colleagues in cabinet next week," Prime Minister Jean Chretien told reporters.
Denmark, the United States and 13 other nations introduced a resolution on Thursday at the U.N. Human Rights Commission in Geneva criticising China's record and seeking reform.

But support for the Western-backed motion seemed to be eroding and Beijing will likely escape censure for the seventh year when the 53-member forum votes next Tuesday. Usual backers of the resolution including France, Germany, Spain and Australia have declined to support it this year.
A Canadian foreign affairs spokeswoman said the issue would come up in informal cabinet discussions, possibly on Monday, ahead of the scheduled vote on Tuesday.

Human rights activists, including an occasional politician from Chretien's own Liberal Party, have criticised the prime minister's policy of trying to engage rather than isolate countries with questionable human rights records.
Chretien has trumpeted the number of contracts signed on trade missions he has led to countries like China and Indonesia and said they are good for Canadian jobs.
China has been applying diplomatic pressure, with commercial overtones, to try to block the resolution.
